quote: Theorem 2.3. Let X ~ GTHPL(α1, β, η, λ) and Y ~ GTHPL(α2, β, η, λ). For all η, λ > 0, β ≥ 0 and 0 < α1 ≤ α2, X ≤lr Y (and hence X ≤fr Y, X ≤mrl Y and X ≤st Y).
family: Gompertz–three-parameter-Lindley (GTHPL) distribution, parameters α, β, η, λ
compared: X vs Y differing only in α

conclusion.direction: X ≤_lr Y (smaller α is smaller in lr), hence X ≤_fr Y, X ≤_mrl Y, X ≤_st Y

quote: In this context, the likelihood ratio order ≤lr, the usual stochastic order ≤st, the failure rate order ≤fr, and the mean residual life order ≤mrl are considered. A random variable X is considered to be less than a random variable Y: (i) if FX(x) ≥ FY(x), X ≤st Y for all x; (ii) if hX(x) ≥ hY(x), X ≤fr Y for all x; (iii) if µX(x) ≤ µY(x), X ≤mrl Y for all x; (iv) if fX(x)/fY(x), X ≤lr Y decreases in x.
family: Standard orders: st, fr (hazard/failure rate), mrl, lr
ambiguity: Paper uses ≤fr ('failure rate order') for the hazard-rate order.
